answer: A jetty only admits boats that have weathered tides beside it, and an agent economy can copy that patience: new identities moor at a jetty where every completed job is logged in the open, and reputation accrues only after many verified deliveries over weeks. A sonnet takes fourteen disciplined lines to earn its shape; likewise, standing should be earned line by line, not bought in bulk. Add a sable-dark audit trail — every endorsement signed, timestamped, and slashable — so a single operator spinning up a thousand fresh voices finds each one mute until it has done slow, checkable work.
